title: Mitchell Starc Takes Ten Wickets as Australia Salvage Bangladesh Series 1-1
excerpt: The left-arm pacer's devastating 6-12 and 4-39 anchored Australia's innings victory in Mackay, but Bangladesh leave their first Australian tour in 23 years with heads held high after a historic win in Darwin.
body:
• Mitchell Starc took 10 wickets (6-12 and 4-39) as Australia thrashed Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs in the second Test at Mackay, leveling the two-match series 1-1.
  • Bangladesh's remarkable series included a stunning nine-wicket win in the opening Test at Darwin — their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil — during their first tour of Australia in 23 years.
  • Shoriful Islam's 7-48 in Mackay was the best innings haul by a Bangladesh bowler in an away Test, demonstrating the growing depth of South Asian fast bowling.
  • The pre-match debate over dropping Nathan Lyon for a four-pace attack was resolved when Australia retained their veteran spinner, who took three wickets including the match-clinching dismissals.

Starc's Devastating Spell

Mitchell Starc needed just 22 balls to take five wickets as Bangladesh were bowled out for 64 on day one of the second Test at Mackay's Great Barrier Reef Arena — Australia's newest Test venue. The left-arm pacer struck with the first delivery of the match, removing opener Shadman Islam, and proceeded to dismantle the top order with swing and seam that left Bangladesh reeling at 12 for five after just 6.4 overs.

Starc finished with figures of 6-12 in the first innings, recording the sixth-fastest five-wicket haul in Test history. He already held the record for the fastest — 15 balls — set against West Indies in Kingston last year. Captain Pat Cummins complemented Starc's assault with 3-25 on a bouncy pitch deliberately prepared to resemble a typical Gabba wicket.

Bangladesh Hit Back Through Shoriful

If the first session belonged entirely to Australia, the recalled Shoriful Islam ensured Bangladesh would not go quietly. The 25-year-old left-arm pacer, returning after missing the Darwin Test with a hamstring strain, produced a career-best 7-48 that tore through Australia's batting order.

""We're trying to give it another day to see whether it's four quicks or a spinner."

Shoriful bowled opener Travis Head for 22, dismissed the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne for four, and trapped Steve Smith lbw for 44, ending a 77-run partnership with Cameron Green. His performance represented the best innings figures by a Bangladesh bowler in an away Test — a record that underlines the team's growing fast-bowling depth.

Eighteen wickets fell on a chaotic first day, with Australia limping to 165 for eight at stumps. Cameron Green, who scored 67, was the only batter on either side to pass 50 in the match, as the pace-friendly surface made batting a survival exercise.

The Lyon Debate

Before the match, Australia's selection became its own storyline. Captain Cummins admitted the team was weighing whether to drop veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon — a near-permanent fixture in Australia's Test side since 2011 — in favor of a four-quick attack featuring Scott Boland.

"We're trying to give it another day to see whether it's four quicks or a spinner. It's largely conditions based." — Pat Cummins, Australia captain

After a further assessment of the pitch during Friday's practice session, coach Andrew McDonald decided to retain Lyon. The decision was vindicated when Lyon took three wickets across both innings, including Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto for 31 in the second innings, and claimed the final two wickets in three balls to seal Australia's comprehensive victory.

Lyon also contributed a useful 32 not out with the bat, putting on a 24-run last-wicket stand with Josh Hazlewood that stretched Australia's lead to 146.

Bangladesh's Historic Tour

While the Mackay result returned to the expected script, Bangladesh's overall tour was anything but predictable. In Darwin, they had piled on 426 in their first innings — their highest total on Australian soil — before bowling Australia out twice to seal a nine-wicket victory. It was Bangladesh's first-ever Test win in Australia and one of the most significant results in the country's cricket history.

The series ended 1-1, and Bangladesh captain Shanto acknowledged the learning curve. "It was challenging for us. But as a team if we want to go forward we need to address these conditions and I think this experience will help us moving forward," he said.

For the South Asian cricket community, Bangladesh's competitiveness against the world's top-ranked Test team signals a broader trend. Their fast-bowling stocks, long considered a weakness, now include genuine pace threats who can exploit conditions worldwide. Shoriful was beaming after the match as he swapped notes with Starc, a moment that captured the mutual respect between two left-arm pacers at different stages of their careers.

What It Means for Cricket

Starc's performance moved him to 445 Test wickets, placing him 10th on the all-time list. Already the most prolific left-arm pace bowler in Test history, the 36-year-old remains central to cricket's competitive landscape, particularly for Asian teams preparing to face Australia in future series.

"Nathan Lyon didn't remind me that I've just stepped on the first rung of the ladder and he's still up there looking down on me," Starc said with a wry grin, referencing Lyon's position four spots ahead on the all-time wickets list.

The series also validated Mackay as a viable Test venue, though the extreme pace and bounce of the pitch — which produced 30 wickets in fewer than five sessions — raised questions about the balance between bat and ball on a surface designed to maximize fast-bowling impact.
nri_angle: Bangladesh's competitive showing against Australia highlights the growing strength of South Asian cricket, with their first-ever Test win on Australian soil a landmark moment for the region's cricketing community.
